html:
Nunatsiavut, "our beautiful land", is the self governing region of the Labrador Inuit in northern Labrador, Canada. The Labrador Inuit Land Claims Agreement created it in 2005, and its government sits at Hopedale; Nain is the largest town.

The Labrador Inuit descend from the Thule people, who reached Labrador around the 1400s. They hunted seals, whales and caribou and traded south with Europeans. From 1771 German Moravian missionaries set up stations at Nain, Hopedale, Hebron and elsewhere, and their influence on church, music and schooling is still strong. In 1959 Hebron was closed and its people moved south against their will.

Labrador was part of the Dominion of Newfoundland until it joined Canada in 1949. Neighbours include the Innu inland, the Naskapi to the west, and the Inuit of NunatuKavut to the south. See also Inuit.
